items.title: Multiplicative system in a category
items.statement: Fix a locally small category and a two-sided fraction system: identities/composition, both Ore squares, and both cancellation directions. Use the published definable-class convention; restrict to small categories or supply small cofinal denominator families; do not infer local smallness of localization.

items.title: Localization of a category at a class of morphisms
items.statement: A localization Q inverts S and is universal among functors inverting S, with the category and Q included in the data.

items.title: Left roof representing a localized morphism
items.statement: A left roof X <-s- U -f-> Y represents Q(f)Q(s)^(-1), s in S.

items.title: Common refinement equivalence of roofs
items.statement: Roofs (s,f),(t,g) are equivalent when maps a:V->U,b:V->Uprime satisfy sa=tb in S and fa=gb; a,b need not separately lie in S.

items.title: Roof equivalence is an equivalence relation
items.statement: Common refinement gives a reflexive, symmetric, transitive relation. Transitivity must use Ore and cancellation with the composite denominator, not assume refinement legs lie in S.

items.title: Composition of roofs is well defined
items.statement: Compose via an Ore square f a=t b and denominator s a. Prove independence from the Ore square and both representatives; prove associativity and identity roof laws.

items.title: The calculus of fractions constructs the localization
items.statement: Roof classes form the localization in the supplied size setting; descend F by (s,f) -> F(f)F(s)^(-1). Include equality detection Q(f)=Q(g) iff f u=g u for some denominator u and the dual roof presentation.

items.title: Quasi isomorphisms contain identities and are closed under composition
items.statement: Identities and composites induce cohomology isomorphisms.

items.title: Two out of three for quasi isomorphisms
items.statement: For composable complex maps, if two of f,g,gf are quasi-isomorphisms, so is the third.

items.title: Quasi isomorphisms admit the roof calculus in the homotopy category
items.statement: Quasi-isomorphisms in the cochain homotopy category satisfy both Ore and cancellation axioms, also in each bounded variant. Use cone triangles and Hom exactness; size is a separate standing assumption.

items.title: Derived category of an abelian category
items.statement: Use cochain reindexing of the published K(A); D(A)=K(A)[qis^(-1)]. D-,D+,Db initially localize termwise bounded variants; identification with cohomologically bounded full subcategories is proved later. Use the definable-class convention with the stated denominator smallness condition when asserting Hom sets; for bounded module calculations local smallness is supplied by the later resolution-model equivalence.

items.title: The localization functor sends quasi isomorphisms to isomorphisms
items.statement: Q(s) is invertible for every quasi-isomorphism s, with inverse the reversed roof.

items.title: Cohomology factors through the derived category
items.statement: Each H^n factors uniquely through Q. Once triangulation is established, its long cohomology sequences follow from images of cone triangles (proved in item 17).

items.title: A complex is zero in the derived category exactly when it is acyclic
items.statement: Q(X) is a zero object iff all H^n(X) vanish; use X->0 in one direction and the factored cohomology in the other.

items.title: Addition of roofs makes an additive localization
items.statement: For an additive category, common-denominator addition of roofs is representative-independent and bilinear for composition; Q preserves zero and biproducts.

items.title: Finite roof squares and composable pairs can be cleared
items.statement: A commuting square in a two-sided fraction localization can be replaced by a commuting square in the original category with denominator comparison maps. Likewise clear a composable pair and its composite simultaneously; prove by Ore and cancellation.

references.title: Lemma 4.27.10, complete proof including footnote common denominator construction

items.title: Localized cone triangles satisfy tr one through tr three
items.statement: Isomorphic images of cone triangles satisfy TR1, signed TR2, and TR3: use roofs for completion and the finite roof-clearing lemma to lift the square; obtain the third denominator via cohomology five lemma. The third comparison map is a quasi-isomorphism by the cohomology long exact sequences and five lemma, before triangulation of D is established.

items.title: Localized cone triangles satisfy the octahedral axiom
items.statement: After simultaneous denominator clearing of two composable maps, the published octahedron in K(A) descends to the required octahedron in D(A), with all connecting signs preserved.

items.title: The derived category inherits a triangulated structure
items.statement: Images of cone triangles, closed under isomorphism, give a triangulation and Q is exact. All H^n give the expected long exact sequences.

items.title: The derived category is the verdier quotient by acyclic complexes
items.statement: Define the narrow Verdier quotient by the thick acyclic subcategory using precisely maps with acyclic cone. It is D(A); prove universal factorization for exact functors annihilating acyclics, using Hom exactness to detect invertibility.

items.title: Homotopically projective bounded above complex
items.statement: Define K-projective by Hom_K(P,A[n])=0 for every acyclic A and every n; equivalently the cochain Hom complex is acyclic. Specialize to bounded-above P but do not build boundedness into the general K-projective predicate.

items.title: Homotopically injective bounded below complex
items.statement: Define K-injective dually by Hom_K(A,I[n])=0 for every acyclic A and integer n; emphasize bounded-below I as the licensed replacement case.

items.title: A bounded above complex of projectives is homotopically projective
items.statement: A bounded-above cochain complex of projectives is K-projective: descend from its highest degree, lifting through cycles of the acyclic target. For the countable recursive homotopy construction assume DC, or supply the degreewise lifting choices.

items.title: A bounded below complex of injectives is homotopically injective
items.statement: A bounded-below cochain complex of injectives is K-injective: ascend from its lowest degree, extending residual maps from boundaries of the acyclic source. For the countable recursive homotopy construction assume DC, or supply the degreewise lifting choices.

items.title: Morphisms from a homotopically projective complex need no roof
items.statement: Hom_K(P,X)->Hom_D(P,X) is bijective for K-projective P. Cone Hom exactness gives the unique homotopy-class lift through each denominator.

items.title: Morphisms into a homotopically injective complex need no roof
items.statement: Hom_K(X,I)->Hom_D(X,I) is bijective for K-injective I. Use the dual denominator calculus and Hom exactness. Include the auxiliary splitting of the cone triangle of an outgoing quasi-isomorphism from I, using its retraction and cone matrices (Weibel Exercise10.4.1).

items.title: Brutal truncation of a complex
items.statement: Brutal truncation deletes all terms on one side without correcting the boundary term. In cochains sigma>=n is a subcomplex and sigma<=n a quotient.

references.title: 12.15, all four chain and four cochain truncations

items.title: Canonical truncation of a complex
items.statement: In cochains tau<=n uses ker(d^n) at n and tau>=n uses coker(d^(n-1)) at n; specify induced differentials and natural maps.

references.title: 12.15, all four chain and four cochain truncations

items.title: Canonical truncation is a complex and has the claimed cohomology
items.statement: The canonical truncations are functorial complexes preserving cohomology on the retained side and killing the other; they preserve quasi-isomorphisms and so descend to D.

references.title: 12.15, all four chain and four cochain truncations

items.title: Canonical truncations fit a distinguished triangle
items.statement: First prove every short exact sequence of complexes yields a distinguished triangle by the quasi-isomorphism Cone(inclusion)->quotient. Then X/tau<=n X -> tau>=n+1 X is a quasi-isomorphism, giving the truncation triangle and its adjacent-cohomology-layer variants.

items.title: Bounded derived localizations embed fully faithfully
items.statement: The bounded localizations embed fully faithfully in D(A); their essential images are exactly the complexes with the corresponding cohomological bounds. Truncate roof representatives and equality witnesses, using both roof orientations.

items.title: Bounded above complexes admit projective replacements
items.statement: Enough projectives gives each bounded-above complex a termwise epic quasi-isomorphism from a bounded-above projective complex, preserving its upper bound. Descending induction chooses an epimorphism onto X^(n-1) fibre-product over X^n with ker(d_P^n); verify surjectivity on cycles and isomorphisms in higher cohomology. Assume DC for the countable inductive choices, or supply the successive epimorphisms as data.

items.title: Bounded below complexes admit injective replacements
items.statement: Dual ascending pushout construction gives a termwise monic bounded-below injective replacement preserving the lower bound. Objectwise existence assumes DC for countable inductive choices, or supplied successive monomorphisms; a class-indexed replacement assignment remains supplied data.

items.title: Projective complexes model the bounded above derived category
items.statement: With supplied projective replacements, K-(Proj A)->D-(A) is fully faithful and essentially surjective and admits the supplied quasi-inverse; cones and shifts stay in the model.

items.title: Injective complexes model the bounded below derived category
items.statement: With supplied injective replacements, K+(Inj A)->D+(A) is the dual equivalence of triangulated categories. After canonical truncations are available, verify that bounded-below acyclic inputs suffice to test K-injectivity of a bounded-below complex (Yekutieli13.1.2).

items.title: Ext is hom in the derived category
items.statement: For objects M,N and n>=0, classical Ext^n(M,N) is naturally Hom_D(M,N[n]) whenever enough projectives or enough injectives and the relevant resolution data are supplied; either model suffices, not both simultaneously.

items.title: Yoneda product is composition in the derived category
items.statement:
Assume DC, set-sized extension classes, and enough projectives with supplied resolutions, or dually enough injectives with supplied resolutions. Normalize the image of a short extension to be its connecting arrow in the cone convention of this page, and the image of a higher extension to be the shifted composite of the connecting arrows of its short exact pieces. With this normalization the Yoneda-class bijection is $\operatorname{YExt}^n(M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_D(M,N[n])$ for $n\geq1$. If $\alpha\in\operatorname{YExt}^p(M,L)$ and $\beta\in\operatorname{YExt}^q(L,N)$, their splice corresponds to $\beta[p]\alpha:M\to N[p+q]$; degree-zero maps act by pullback and pushout, with identity units.

In particular, for $e:0\to A\to Z\to B\to0$ and $e':0\to B\xrightarrow u Z'\to C\to0$, the splice is zero in $\operatorname{Ext}^2(C,A)$ if and only if there is an extension $0\to A\to W\to Z'\to0$ whose pullback along $u$ is $e$. Equivalently there is a commutative diagram of these two rows, with vertical maps $1_A,Z\to W,u$, whose middle and right columns are $0\to Z\to W\to C\to0$ and $0\to B\to Z'\to C\to0$.

items.title: Canonical t structure on a derived category
items.statement: State all t-structure axioms and the heart inside the definition: shift inclusions, Hom(D<=0,D>=1)=0 and decomposition triangles. Define the canonical candidate by cohomology vanishing.

references.title: Lecture 3, section 3, definition and Main example, pp. 28–29

items.title: The canonical pair is a t structure
items.statement: The canonical candidate is a t-structure. To prove orthogonality replace the target by tau>=1 and a left-roof source by tau<=0, so every chain map is zero; shift closure and decomposition use the canonical truncation-triangle theorem. Include the same canonical structure on D-, D+, Db. The roof argument also proves Hom_D(X,Y[n])=0 for n<b-a and Hom_D(X,Y[b-a])=Hom_A(H^a X,H^b Y) when X has no cohomology above a and Y has none below b.

references.title: Lecture 3, section 3, definition and Main example, pp. 28–29

items.title: The heart of the canonical t structure is equivalent to the original abelian category
items.statement: The degree-zero embedding A->D identifies A with the heart; H^0 is its inverse. Double truncation reduces roofs between degree-zero objects to ordinary arrows.

items.title: Left total derived functor on the bounded above derived category
items.statement: For additive F and supplied projective replacements define LF(X)=QF(P_X), including augmentation LF Q -> QF and the terminal universal comparison property.

references.title: 10.5.1–10.5.8, pp. 391–393; restrict to supplied replacement data

items.title: Left total derived functor is independent of the supplied projective replacement up to unique natural isomorphism
items.statement: Two supplied replacement systems give a natural comparison isomorphism unique among comparisons compatible with their augmentations; do not assert uniqueness of arbitrary natural automorphisms.

references.title: 10.5.1–10.5.8, pp. 391–393; restrict to supplied replacement data

items.title: Existence of the bounded above left total derived functor
items.statement: The replacement recipe is a functor D-(A)->D-(B) with the left total-derived universal property. Additivity suffices; right exactness is needed to identify H^0 with F.

references.title: 10.5.1–10.5.8, pp. 391–393; restrict to supplied replacement data

items.title: Right total derived functor on the bounded below derived category
items.statement: For additive F and supplied injective replacements define RF(X)=QF(I_X), with QF -> RF Q and the initial universal comparison property.

references.title: 10.5.1–10.5.8, pp. 391–393; restrict to supplied replacement data

items.title: Existence of the bounded below right total derived functor
items.statement: The dual bounded-below construction is a functor D+(A)->D+(B); prove change-of-injective-replacement independence and uniqueness relative to coaugmentations, and the universal property. The supplied construction before Q_B also factors through K+(B), and model values agree under the bounded embedding in D.

references.title: 10.5.1–10.5.8, pp. 391–393; restrict to supplied replacement data

items.title: Total derived functors send distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles
items.statement: LF and RF preserve distinguished triangles with the shift comparisons transported through the bounded model equivalences. For an exact F, the termwise functor already descends and its derived comparison is an isomorphism.

references.title: 10.5.1–10.5.8, pp. 391–393; restrict to supplied replacement data

items.title: Classical derived functors are the cohomology objects of the total derived functor
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Dependent Choice. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive between abelian categories. On the left assume enough projectives and supplied bounded-above projective replacements, and on the right enough injectives and supplied bounded-below injective replacements. On the respective domains $D^-(\mathcal A)$ and $D^+(\mathcal A)$, $H^{-n}(LF(M[0]))=L_nF(M)$ and $H^n(RF(M[0]))=R^nF(M)$ for $n\geq0$, relative to the same resolution data, naturally. To compare the classical cycle-lifting connecting maps with the triangle connecting maps for the page's cone convention, multiply these degree-$n$ identifications by $(-1)^n$; the resulting natural isomorphisms commute with connecting maps. The left comparison with $F$ in degree zero is an isomorphism when $F$ is right exact; the right comparison is an isomorphism when $F$ is left exact. Conversely such a natural degree-zero comparison isomorphism forces that side-exactness.

The functor $LF$ preserves upper cohomological bounds and $RF$ preserves lower bounds. The truncation maps induce $H^iLF(X)\cong H^iLF(\tau^{\geq a}X)$ for $i\geq a$, and $H^iRF(\tau^{\leq a}X)\cong H^iRF(X)$ for $i\leq a$. On objects of $\mathcal A$, $H^0LF$ is right exact and $H^0RF$ is left exact.

For left exact $F$, call $M$ right $F$-acyclic when $F(M)[0]\to RF(M[0])$ is invertible. This holds iff $R^nF(M)=0$ for all $n>0$. In $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$, right acyclicity of $(A,C)$ implies that of $B$; that of $(A,B)$ implies that of $C$; that of $(B,C)$ together with epic $F(B)\to F(C)$ implies that of $A$. In each case $0\to F(A)\to F(B)\to F(C)\to0$ is exact. Dually, for right exact $F$, left acyclicity is equivalent to $L_nF(M)=0$ for $n>0$: the pairs $(A,C)$ and $(B,C)$ imply respectively $B$ and $A$, while $(A,B)$ implies $C$ provided $F(A)\to F(B)$ is monic, again with the resulting short exact sequence. Under DC, both supplied object-resolution data, and the respective enough-projective/right-exact or enough-injective/left-exact hypotheses, these are the classical universal delta functors.

references.title: 10.5.1–10.5.8, pp. 391–393; restrict to supplied replacement data

items.title: Bounded above flat tensor complexes preserve quasi isomorphisms
items.statement: Tensoring a bounded-above acyclic cochain complex with a bounded-above flat complex gives an acyclic finite-diagonal total complex. Prove by finite cycle elimination along diagonals after reindexing; deduce invariance under quasi-isomorphisms in the other variable and balance via the two-replacement diagram. No spectral-sequence prerequisite. Reindex to chain degrees and use the dual of the published finite-diagonal assembly argument; explain the dualization and signs explicitly.

references.title: 10.6.1–10.6.4 and Exercise 10.6.1, p. 395; elementary finite-diagonal replacement for spectral sequence proof

items.title: Derived tensor product in the bounded above setting
items.statement: For bounded-above right and left R-complexes N and M, N tensor^L_R M is represented using a supplied projective replacement of either variable. The common two-replacement model gives the natural balancing isomorphism.

references.title: 10.6.1–10.6.4 and Exercise 10.6.1, p. 395; elementary finite-diagonal replacement for spectral sequence proof

items.title: Homology of the derived tensor product is tor
items.statement: For modules in degree zero, H^(-n)(N tensor^L_R M)=Tor_n^R(N,M); no unrestricted hypertor assertion is needed.

references.title: 10.6.1–10.6.4 and Exercise 10.6.1, p. 395; elementary finite-diagonal replacement for spectral sequence proof

items.title: Derived hom in the bounded setting
items.statement: For M in D-(A) and N in D+(A), define RHom in D+(Ab) via Hom(P_M,N) if enough projectives or Hom(M,I_N) if enough injectives. Prove invariance in both variables by K-orthogonality. When both exist compare through Hom(P_M,I_N).

items.title: Cohomology of derived hom is ext
items.statement: For degree-zero M,N, H^n RHom(M,N)=classical Ext^n(M,N); more generally in the declared mixed bounded range it is Hom_D(M,N[n]).

items.title: Splitting a bounded complex by vanishing higher Ext
items.statement: With supplied projective or injective resolutions, if X is cohomologically bounded and Ext^p(H^i X,H^j X)=0 for p>=2 and i>j, then X is isomorphic to the finite sum of H^i(X)[-i]. Prove the zero-connecting-map splitting criterion inline using Hom exactness and the split triangle, then induct on cohomological amplitude. Inline corollary: if Ext^2 vanishes for every pair, all bounded complexes split; propagate vanishing via Yoneda splicing. The splitting is not claimed canonical.
For every quasi-isomorphism s, Q(s) is literally an identity. Refute with -1 on Z[0], detected by H^0.

items.statement: Two roofs with the same right arrow necessarily agree. Use numerator id on Z[0] and denominators id,-id, giving id,-id in D.

references.title: Boundary check against the licensed construction

items.statement: Q:K(A)->D(A) is always an equivalence. The nonsplit exact complex 0->Z->Z->Z/2->0 is zero only in D.

references.title: Boundary check against the licensed construction

items.statement: Every unbounded complex of projectives is K-projective. Over Z/4 use the doubly infinite multiplication-by-2 complex: acyclic, but the identity cannot be dh+hd since its components would be even.

items.statement: Brutal and canonical truncation coincide. For Z --2--> Z in degrees 0,1, sigma<=0 is Z[0] whereas tau<=0 is zero.

references.title: Boundary check against the licensed construction

items.statement: Enough injectives alone licenses computing unbounded RF by arbitrary termwise injective replacements. Over R=Z/4 the periodic 2 complex is an acyclic complex of injectives but Hom_R(R/2,-) gives zero differentials and nonzero terms. Prove R is injective by Baer on its three ideals. This refutes the asserted recipe, not a blanket nonexistence theorem.

items.statement: A replacement model LF is literally canonical without supplied replacement data. Adding the contractible identity complex to a chosen projective replacement changes the literal representative while preserving its derived isomorphism class.

items.statement: Assume Dependent Choice and supplied projective resolution data on $\mathbf{Ab}$, with $U$ below supplied for $\mathbb Z/2$, and set-sized Yoneda extension classes as in [F2]. The nonsplit extension $0\to\mathbb Z\xrightarrow2\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z/2\to0$ is represented in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$ by the roof $\mathbb Z/2[0]\xleftarrow sU\xrightarrow f\mathbb Z[1]$, where $U=(\mathbb Z\xrightarrow2\mathbb Z)$ in degrees $-1,0$, $s^0$ is reduction modulo two, and $f^{-1}=1$. Its class generates $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathbb Z/2,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z/2$.
The nonsplit exact three-term complex Z->2 Z->Z/2 is acyclic and hence zero in D, but any contraction would split the quotient.
The augmentation (Z->2 Z)->Z/2[0] is inverted by the roof Z/2[0]<-(Z->2 Z)->id (Z->2 Z).
Compute Hom_D(Z/m[0],Z/n[1])=Z/gcd(m,n), m,n>0, through the two-term free resolution and its Hom complex.
Compute all four truncations at 0 of Z->2 Z in degrees 0,1, distinguishing kernel/cokernel from brutal boundary terms.

references.title: 12.15, all four chain and four cochain truncations

items.statement: For X=(Z/4->2 Z/4) in degrees 0,1, display tau<=0 X -> X -> tau>=1 X -> tau<=0 X[1] and obtain its maps via the quotient complex.
For m,n>0, model Z/m tensor^L_Z Z/n by Z/n->m Z/n in degrees -1,0. H^-1 and H^0 are Z/gcd(m,n); other cohomology vanishes.

references.title: 10.6.1–10.6.4 and Exercise 10.6.1, p. 395; elementary finite-diagonal replacement for spectral sequence proof

items.statement: For m,n>0, RHom_Z(Z/m,Z/n) is Z/n->m Z/n in degrees 0,1. Its two cohomology groups are Z/gcd(m,n).
Over Z/4 the unbounded periodic free complex with d=2 is acyclic but not K-projective: 1=2h+2hprime is impossible modulo 2.
